claims.text: This page explains the LegalQuants /legaldesign skill.
The method begins with the reader, purpose, source record, and communication goal.
The core design judgment is to identify the relationship, select the clearest visual form, and encode that relationship through position and structure.
Every run produces two complete page alternatives in one editable HTML, with export for the selected page and for a reusable template.
The selected client page and reusable design pattern are the two export paths.

evidence.locator: Method specification, intake and source ledger
evidence.detail: The method identifies the audience, purpose, communication goal, source set, assumptions, and known gaps before visual composition begins.

popup.title: Start with the communication problem
popup.lede: The page cannot be designed intelligently until the agent knows who must understand what, and what they should do next.

sections.heading: Reader and action
sections.body: Name the real reader and the decision, task, or understanding the artifact must enable. This determines what leads and how much legal context belongs on the surface.

sections.heading: Controlling record
sections.body: Identify the supplied source, its status, and the material claims it actually supports before selecting a visual form.

sections.heading: Assumptions and gaps
sections.body: State what is inferred or missing. Design can clarify uncertainty; it cannot quietly turn an unsupported premise into a fact.

evidence.detail: The method asks what relationship matters, which visual representation communicates it most effectively, and how position, grouping, scale, or direction will encode that relationship.

popup.title: Make the relationship do the explaining
popup.lede: A polished page is not a collection of decorated facts. Its structure must make the core relationship perceptible at a glance.

sections.heading: What must be communicated?
sections.body: Write the message as a checkable claim and name the relationship inside it: sequence, hierarchy, comparison, containment, priority, or another supported form.

sections.heading: Which visual form fits?
sections.body: Compare a plain sentence or table against two visual candidates. Use a diagram only when geometry makes the relationship clearer.

sections.heading: How is it encoded?
sections.body: Name the position, enclosure, connector, scale, size, or reading order that carries the meaning. Color may label or signal status, but it does not substitute for structure.

evidence.detail: A working artifact contains two materially different complete page approaches. The user edits and selects at page level, exports the selected HTML, or exports both structures as a reusable template.

popup.title: Compare complete pages, not isolated components
popup.lede: Approach A and Approach B are two coherent ways to communicate the same grounded legal answer.

sections.heading: Two information structures
sections.body: The alternatives differ in organizing relationship, section architecture, or reading path. Rewording the same boxes is not a second approach.

sections.heading: One editable product
sections.body: The user can edit page copy, diagram labels, purposeful detail popups, and any express decision response before choosing a page.

sections.heading: Two export paths
sections.body: Export HTML keeps the selected client-facing page. Export template preserves both structures with descriptive placeholders and their design reasoning.

evidence.detail: The agent asks only what the supplied record cannot answer, within a three-question budget.

popup.title: Ask only what the record cannot answer
popup.lede: Good intake reduces ambiguity without making the user design the page for the agent.

sections.heading: Three-question ceiling
sections.body: Missing controlling record, reader and next action, and purpose take priority. Questions already answered by the material are skipped.

sections.heading: The agent owns the message
sections.body: The user supplies context and choices. The agent turns those answers into the communication goal and proposes the page architecture.

evidence.detail: A material-claim ledger separates supported facts, context, popup detail, and substantive omissions.

popup.title: Build the claim ledger before drawing
popup.lede: The ledger is the bridge between legal accuracy and visual hierarchy.

sections.heading: One checkable claim per unit
sections.body: Each fact names its source, placement, and evidence path. A mood or theme does not qualify as a material claim.

sections.heading: Nothing disappears silently
sections.body: Every material point appears on the surface, moves into purposeful detail, or is omitted for a stated substantive reason.

evidence.detail: The agent names the relationship that best carries the legal message before choosing a diagram.

popup.title: Name the relationship that carries the answer
popup.lede: Sequence, hierarchy, comparison, containment, and priority demand different reading paths.

sections.heading: Start with the claim
sections.body: Ask what the reader must perceive between the facts—not which template happens to be available.

sections.heading: Choose one spine
sections.body: A dominant relationship gives the page a clear organizing logic. Supporting components may clarify, but they should not compete with it.

evidence.locator: Method specification, visual form and encoding
evidence.detail: The chosen form must encode the relationship through a perceptible geometric property.

popup.title: Choose the form, then prove its encoding
popup.lede: A diagram earns its place only when its geometry communicates more clearly than a sentence, list, or table.

sections.heading: Compare candidates
sections.body: Consider a plain form and two visual forms. Reject any figure that merely decorates the claim.

sections.heading: State the mechanism
sections.body: Explain exactly how position, enclosure, connector, common scale, or size makes the relationship visible.

evidence.detail: Both approaches cover the same legal record but use materially different information structures.

popup.title: A and B must disagree structurally
popup.lede: The comparison is valuable only when each page offers a coherent alternative reading path.

sections.heading: Same legal meaning
sections.body: Both pages cover the same material claims, qualifications, evidence obligations, and express decisions.

sections.heading: Different organization
sections.body: The organizing relationship, section sequence, or information hierarchy changes. Swapping one chart or recoloring cards does not count.

evidence.locator: Method specification, client and template exports
evidence.detail: Client export keeps the selected page; template export preserves the reusable structures and their reasoning.

popup.title: The selected page travels; the method remains reusable
popup.lede: The two exports serve different audiences without leaking matter-specific content into the reusable version.

sections.heading: Client HTML
sections.body: Keep the selected approach, intended interactions, and saved responses. Remove editor chrome, the unused approach, and authoring rationale.

sections.heading: Reusable template
sections.body: Keep both structures and replace matter content with descriptive placeholders so the next user can understand how the pattern works.
